question_bank.stem: A single workflow already uses several prompts and tools. According to the lecture, when does moving to multiple agents become especially attractive?

options.text: When independent specialized tasks can run in parallel rather than waiting on one monolithic controller.
When every task must happen in one fixed serial order so the system avoids any parallel execution.
When the main goal is to remove specialization and make every subtask use the exact same shared prompt.
When the workflow has no reusable pieces and every team needs a completely different implementation from scratch.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture says multi-agent systems become especially useful when parts of the work can happen in parallel.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Opening multi-agent slide asks why multiple agents are needed and frames parallelism as the central advantage.

question_bank.stem: Why did the lecture highlight reuse as another reason to build specialized agents?

options.text: Because reuse guarantees that all teams will share the same user interface and never need orchestration.
Because one agent built for a specialized function can be reused across multiple products or teams.
Because reuse eliminates the need for evaluation once an agent has been deployed in one workflow.
Because reuse means every specialized agent automatically learns from every other agent's memory without coordination.

question_bank.rationale: The instructor explicitly says an agent can be reused across teams or contexts once built for a specialized task.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Multi-agent discussion remains on the opening rationale slide while reuse is introduced alongside parallelism.

question_bank.stem: In the smart-home example, what role does the orchestrator agent play?

options.text: It replaces all specialized agents so the system can avoid any hierarchical structure.
It stores only archival memory while every other agent handles all user interaction directly.
It serves as the main communication point with the user and delegates work to specialized agents.
It acts only as a payment tool so that non-financial agents never need to authenticate users.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture describes a hierarchical pattern in which the user mainly interacts with an orchestrator that coordinates specialists.

source_ref.evidence_span: What is exactly the orchestrator doing?

frame_evidence.visual_description: Smart-home multi-agent example leads into a hierarchical pattern where one orchestration layer coordinates domain agents.

question_bank.stem: Compared with one large monolithic agent, what practical engineering advantage of multi-agent workflows did the lecture emphasize at the end?

options.text: They always reduce the total number of model calls, because every specialized agent shares the same hidden computation.
They make system design deterministic, because specialization removes ambiguity from all user requests.
They remove the need for orchestration, because any group of agents will self-organize without explicit coordination.
They can be easier to debug and can parallelize work more naturally across specialized components.

question_bank.rationale: The lecture closes by citing debugging and parallelization as practical advantages of multi-agent structures.

frame_evidence.visual_description: Closing discussion on multi-agent organization patterns summarizes benefits such as easier debugging and parallel work.
